title: Trade Unions
summary: What trade unions are, their history and role in South Africa, collective bargaining, workers' rights under labour laws, and the advantages and disadvantages of unions.

notes.text: An organisation of workers who join together to protect and improve their wages, working conditions and rights.

One worker on their own has little power when negotiating with an employer. Workers in a union act **together**, which gives them much more bargaining power. Members pay a monthly **membership fee (subscription)**, and elect **shop stewards** to represent them at the workplace.
Trade unions in South African history

items: In 1919 **Clements Kadalie** founded the **Industrial and Commercial Workers' Union (ICU)**, one of the first large black trade unions in Africa.
During apartheid, black unions were not legally recognised until **1979**, after the Wiehahn Commission, although workers organised major strikes, such as the 1973 Durban strikes.
**COSATU** (Congress of South African Trade Unions), formed in **1985**, played a major role in the struggle against apartheid.
Today major federations include COSATU, FEDUSA, NACTU and SAFTU. Large unions include NUM (mineworkers), SADTU (teachers), NUMSA (metalworkers) and NEHAWU (health and public servants).
**Collective bargaining**: negotiating with employers about wages, hours, leave and benefits.
Protecting members from **unfair dismissal** and discrimination.
Representing members in **disciplinary hearings** and disputes.
Influencing government policy on labour and economic issues.

rows: Every worker has the right to fair labour practices, to form and join a trade union, and to strike
Sets rules for collective bargaining, strikes and dispute resolution; established the **CCMA** (Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration)
Sets minimum conditions: working hours (45 hours a week), overtime, annual leave, sick leave, maternity leave
Prohibits unfair discrimination and promotes equal opportunities
Sets a minimum hourly wage for most workers

items: The union presents its demands (e.g. a 9% wage increase).
The two sides negotiate to reach a compromise.
If they cannot agree, a **dispute** is declared and referred to the CCMA or a bargaining council for **conciliation**.
If conciliation fails, workers may go on a **protected (legal) strike** after giving notice. Employers may respond with a **lock-out**.

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: Strikes must be **peaceful**. Violence, intimidation and damage to property are illegal and can harm workers, businesses and the economy.

rows: Strikes cause lost wages and production
Very high wage demands may lead businesses to cut jobs or use machines

questions.prompt: In which year was COSATU formed?
Which union was founded by Clements Kadalie in 1919? (abbreviation)
According to the Basic Conditions of Employment Act, what is the maximum number of ordinary working hours per week?
What is the elected union representative at a workplace called?
The right to strike includes the right to damage property.
Match each law to what it does.

pairs.right: Rules for bargaining and strikes; set up the CCMA
Sets the lowest legal hourly wage

questions.prompt: Explain THREE functions of trade unions.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): collective bargaining; protection from unfair dismissal; health and safety; representing members in hearings; educating members; influencing policy

questions.prompt: Discuss TWO advantages and TWO disadvantages of trade unions for the economy.
questions.memo:
Advantages (1 each): better wages increase spending; safer workplaces; stability through bargaining
Disadvantages (1 each): strikes reduce production; job losses from high wage demands; violence scares investors
